338214.title: The characterization of MDS-PIR capacity-achieving codes
338214.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $[n,k]$ code, and let $d_s^{\mathcal{C}}$ denote the quantity appearing in the necessary condition

$$
d_s^{\mathcal{C}}\geq\frac{n}{k}s,\quad\forall\,s\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
$$

An MDS-PIR capacity-achieving matrix $\bm{\Lambda}_{\kappa,\nu}(\mathcal{C})$ has parameters satisfying $\frac{\kappa}{\nu}=\frac{k}{n}$. **MDS-PIR characterization conjecture.** Such a matrix exists if and only if

$$
d_s^{\mathcal{C}}\geq\frac{n}{k}s,\quad\forall\,s\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
$$

The condition is necessary for the existence of an MDS-PIR capacity-achieving matrix. Exhaustive searches for parameters up to length $11$, with the stated exceptions $[n,k]=[10,5]$ and $[n,k]=[11,4\leq k\leq 7]$, found a matrix whenever the condition held, but sufficiency remains open in general.

338260.title: Catalan graph determinant conjecture
338260.statement:
Let $CG_n$ be the Catalan graph, and let

$$
\Gamma=\{11,13,15,23,33,51,61,63\}.
$$

**Catalan graph determinant conjecture.** The determinant satisfies

$$
\det(CG_n)=0
$$

if and only if $n\ge6$ is even or $n\in\Gamma$. The paper proves the even-order case $\det(CG_{2n})=0$ for $n\ge3$ and reports computational evidence for the exceptional set $\Gamma$; the stated if-and-only-if classification remains conjectural in the supplied text.

338569.title: The vanishing proportion conjecture for magic $n_3$-configurations
338569.statement:
An $n_3$-configuration is a $3$-uniform configuration with $n$ points and $n$ lines, in which every point lies on three lines and every line contains three points. Call such a configuration **magic** over an abelian group if its incidence matrix admits a labeling by elements of the group satisfying the magic condition on every line. **Vanishing proportion conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\text{\# of $n_3$-configs magic over some group}}{\text{\# of $n_3$-configs}} \to 0.
$$

The conjecture is suggested by computations for the known complete lists of $n_3$-configurations with $7\leq n\leq 14$ and by the increasing prevalence of forbidden substructures, including collections of parallel lines, as $n$ grows.

339411.title: Disk conjecture for the roots of the descent polynomial
339411.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite subset of the positive integers, let $m$ be the maximal element of $I\cup\{0\}$, and let $d(I,z)$ be the descent polynomial associated with $I$. For a root $z_0\in\mathbb C$ of this polynomial, consider the disk whose diameter has endpoints $-1$ and $m$.

**Disk conjecture.** If

$$
d(I,z_0)=0,
$$

then

$$
\left|z_0-\frac{m-1}{2}\right|\le\frac{m+1}{2}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by numerical computations for $m\le 13$, the case $|I|=1$, and a result concerning real roots. It simultaneously implies the two previously discussed bounds, but the source does not state that it has been resolved.

339492.title: The closedness and value conjecture for the degree-three density constant
339492.statement:
Let $d$ denote the degree of a Cayley digraph, and let $Delta_3$ and $Delta_3'$ be the associated density constants introduced in the paper. **Degree-three density conjecture.** The degree $d=3$ is closed and

$$
\Delta_3=\Delta_3'=\frac{21}{250}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by numerical evidence comparing the extremal function $\kappa(3,n)$ with the lower bound $\ell'(3,n)$, including computed examples of dilated Cayley digraphs. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

341618.title: Shifted Hecke insertion conjecture for involution words
341618.statement:
Let $v$ and $w$ be **involution words**, and let $\overset{\textsf{O}}\sim$ denote the shifted Hecke equivalence relation. The shifted Hecke insertion algorithm assigns to each word $u$ a tableau $P_{\textsf{O}}(u)$. **Shifted Hecke insertion conjecture.** If

$$
v\overset{\textsf{O}}\sim w,
$$

then

$$
P_{\textsf{O}}(v)=P_{\textsf{O}}(w).
$$

The claim concerns the converse to the already established implication from equal insertion tableaux to equivalence. It is supported by computations and is also stated as Conjecture 5.13 in work of Hamaker, Marberg, and Pawlowski.

341964.title: The crossing-number conjecture for Sunlet–Star Cartesian products
341964.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ be the Sunlet graph on $2n$ vertices, obtained by attaching $n$ pendant edges to the cycle $C_n$, and let $K_{1,m}$ be the star graph on $m+1$ vertices. For a graph $G$, write $cr(G)$ for its crossing number. **Sunlet–Star crossing-number conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$ and $m\geq 1$,

$$
cr(\mathcal{S}_n\Box K_{1,m})=n\frac{m(m-1)}{2}.
$$

The formula is established in the paper for $m=1,2,3$ and is supported computationally for $n,m\leq 20$, but remains conjectural for general $m$.

342411.title: Nonexistence of infinite uniquely-Wilf classes containing all permutations of length three
342411.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be a class of permutations, and let ${\mathcal{C}}_3$ denote its permutations of length three. Let ${\mathcal{S}}_3$ be the set of all permutations of length three. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no infinite uniquely-Wilf classes ${\mathcal{C}}$ with

$$
{\mathcal{C}}_3={\mathcal{S}}_3.
$$

This would complete the classification of infinite uniquely-Wilf classes in the remaining cases where ${\mathcal{C}}_3={\mathcal{S}}_3$ and the number of permutations of length four is $22$, $23$, or $24$; the paper explains that these cases remain open because the available computational constraints were insufficient.

343098.title: Exact unconnected-graph count conjecture for linear equational graphs
343098.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $L(p)$ be defined by

$$
L(p)=\begin{cases}(p-1)/4&\text{if }p\equiv1\pmod 8,\\(p+1)/4&\text{if }p\equiv3\pmod 8,\\(p+3)/4&\text{if }p\equiv5\pmod 8,\\(p-3)/4&\text{if }p\equiv7\pmod 8,\end{cases}
$$

and let $U_1(p)$ denote the number of unconnected graphs in the linear family. **Exact-count conjecture.** For any prime $p>31$, $U_1(p)=L(p)$. The computations reported in the source support this equality for the tested primes up to $3041$, but no proof or resolution is given.

343100.title: Exact unconnected-graph count conjecture for cubic equational graphs
343100.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime satisfying $3\nmid p-1$, let $L(p)$ be the piecewise function defined by

$$
L(p)=\begin{cases}(p-1)/4&\text{if }p\equiv1\pmod 8,\\(p+1)/4&\text{if }p\equiv3\pmod 8,\\(p+3)/4&\text{if }p\equiv5\pmod 8,\\(p-3)/4&\text{if }p\equiv7\pmod 8,\end{cases}
$$

and let $U_3(p)$ denote the number of unconnected graphs ${\mathcal G}(\lambda,X^3+a)$ with $\lambda\in{\mathbb N}_p$ and $a\in{\mathbb F}_p^*$. **Cubic exact-count conjecture.** For any prime $p>31$ satisfying $3\nmid p-1$, $U_3(p)=L(p)$. The source reports computational verification for the relevant primes up to $3041$, but provides no proof or resolution.

343101.title: Two-component conjecture for unconnected cubic equational graphs
343101.statement: Let $p$ be a prime with $p\ge5$ satisfying $3\nmid p-1$, and let ${\mathcal G}(\lambda,X^3+a)$ be a cubic equational graph over ${\mathbb F}_p$, where $\lambda\in{\mathbb N}_p$ and $a\ne0$. **Cubic two-component conjecture.** If ${\mathcal G}(\lambda,X^3+a)$ is unconnected, then it has exactly two connected components. The claim is based on computations through $p=3041$ and is not resolved in the source.

344001.title: The classification conjecture for six-element extreme sets in cyclic groups
344001.statement:
Let $A$ be a six-element subset of a cyclic group. Two subsets are considered equivalent when one is obtained from the other by a group homomorphism and a translation.

**Six-element classification conjecture.** The only six-element extreme sets in cyclic groups are $\mathbb Z_6$, the set $\{0,1,2,3,4,7\}\subset\mathbb Z_{10}$, and their images under group homomorphism and translation.

The claim is motivated by the examples and computational evidence in the paper. The supplied text gives no proof or disproof, so the classification remains open.

344132.title: The nonexistence conjecture for extremal square-free words over four-letter alphabets
344132.statement: A square-free word is a word containing no factor of the form $uu$ with $u$ nonempty, and an **extremal square-free word** is a square-free word that cannot be extended by inserting a single letter in any position while remaining square-free. **Extremal-word nonexistence conjecture.** There are no extremal square-free words over a $4$-letter alphabet. The conjecture is motivated by a computer search that found no extremal words over four letters of length up to $1000$. If true, every square-free word over four letters could be extended by inserting a letter, and this would imply the corresponding infinitude conjecture for nonchalant words over four-letter alphabets.

344430.title: The periodic perturbation conjecture for maximum-coefficient locations
344430.statement: Let $\mathbf{B}$ be the base vector, and let $\mathbf{u}_r$ and $\mathbf{v}_r$ denote the perturbation vectors defined by the rows of the source's tables. **Periodic perturbation conjecture.** For any $i>j\geq 1$, the $i$-th and $j$-th rows appearing in the table of words and beyond are associated, respectively, with $\mathbf{B}+\mathbf{u}_{i-1\pmod{11}}$ for the $1\pmod 4$ words and $\mathbf{B}+\mathbf{v}_{j\pmod{11}}$ for the $3\pmod 4$ words. The conjecture is an observed vector pattern intended to explain the periodic behavior of the differences $E_n$; the source provides computational and tabular evidence but no proof.

344665.title: Bajnok and Brinkmann's six-exception conjecture for triangle-free subcubic graphs
344665.statement:
Let $F_{11}$, $F_{14}^{(1)}$, $F_{14}^{(2)}$, $F_{19}^{(1)}$, $F_{19}^{(2)}$, and $F_{22}$ denote the six specified forbidden graphs. **Bajnok and Brinkmann's conjecture.** There are exactly six $2$-connected triangle-free subcubic graphs $G$ satisfying

$$
\alpha(G)<\frac{3}{8}n,
$$

namely $F_{11}$, $F_{14}^{(1)}$, $F_{14}^{(2)}$, $F_{19}^{(1)}$, $F_{19}^{(2)}$, and $F_{22}$. The conjecture asserts that the six graphs found in the cited computer search are the complete list of exceptions. The source gives no resolution status for this conjecture.

344724.title: The h-vector form conjecture for odd cycle toric rings
344724.statement:
Let $C_{2s+1}$ be the cycle graph on $2s+1$ vertices, and let $K[C_{2s+1}]$ denote its toric ring. Write its $h$-vector as a sequence with entries $h_1,h_2,\ldots,h_{s-1}$ appearing in the indicated positions. **The h-vector form conjecture.** The $h$-vector of $K[C_{2s+1}]$ is of the form

$$
(1, h_1, h_2, h_3, \ldots, h_i, \ldots, h_{s-1}, h_{s-1} + (-1)^{s-1}, \ldots, h_i + (-1)^{i}, \ldots, h_3 - 1, h_2 + 1, h_1, 1).
$$

This conjectural form describes the asymmetry of the $h$-vectors of toric rings of odd cycles. The preceding examples for $C_7$, $C_9$, and $C_{11}$ provide computational evidence, but the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

345005.title: Eventual periodicity conjecture for signs of $q$-series coefficients
345005.statement:
The coefficients $a_{r,s,t}(n)$ and $b_{r,s,t}(n)$ are defined by the $q$-series expansions associated with the given parameters $r$, $s$, and $t$. For fixed $r$, $s$, and $t$, consider the signs of these coefficients as $n$ varies.

**Eventual sign-periodicity conjecture.** For given $r$, $s$, and $t$, the signs of $a_{r,s,t}(n)$'s and $b_{r,s,t}(n)$'s are periodic with period $t$ or $2t$ from sufficiently large $n$.

This conjecture is motivated by numerical evidence for the cases $t=5$, $7$, and $11$, where the coefficient signs appear eventually periodic. The paper notes that it is unclear how to prove these sign patterns using $q$-series methods.

348339.title: The uniqueness conjecture for common projective-group degrees
348339.statement:
For integers $n,k\ge 2$ and prime powers $q,r\ge 2$, let ${\rm L}_n(q)$ and ${\rm L}_k(r)$ be projective special linear groups with natural degrees

$$
\frac{q^n-1}{q-1}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{r^k-1}{r-1},
$$
 respectively. A natural degree is common when these two quantities are equal. **The uniqueness conjecture for common projective-group degrees.** Apart from the common degree $31$ arising from ${\rm L}_3(5)$ and ${\rm L}_5(2)$, there are no other natural degrees common to two different projective groups ${\rm L}_n(q)$. The claim is presented as a computationally motivated conjecture and is unresolved in the source.

348918.title: Integer-spectrum conjecture for the n-Queens' graph

349132.title: Generalized Marchal's conjecture for odd-body polygon and figure-eight choreographies
349132.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd number of bodies. Consider the $n$-gon choreography and the $n$-body figure-eight choreography. Two periodic orbits are in the same **continuation class** if one can be reached from the other by continuous variation of the energy.

**Generalized Marchal's conjecture.** For any odd number of bodies, the $n$-gon choreography and the $n$-body figure eight are in the same continuation class.

This generalizes the three-body claim and is motivated by numerical continuations for three and five bodies. The paper presents numerical evidence for odd numbers of bodies from $3$ through $15$, but the assertion remains unproved in general.
